newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil firm, but quiet and lagging crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil firm, but quiet and lagging crude.

text.p: Fuel oil was steady, but the market was quieter as it pondered crude's recent rally amid some doubts whether it could be sustained.
Traders said there was room for fuel to move higher since it remained at a high discount to crude given the time of the year.
High sulphur barges traded sharply higher early with $128 and $128.50 fob ARA done, but prices then slipped with most deals concluded in a range of $126-127.
"Prices could have fallen more if it had not been for good bunker requirement," said one trader who said as low as $124 was talked.

Low sulphur barges were even quieter with most October business done, but a 600 tonne barge was sold at $132 fob ARA. High sulphur cracked cargoes were broadly steady after Monday's hike with a 2.1 percent sulphur content cargo sold today at $126.75 cif Pembroke. The cargo orginated in Brofjorden.

Physical low sulphur cargoes were close to swaps numbers of $128-129 fob NWE. "Crude has given little strength to low sulphur," said one trader who estimated cargoes would have to be around $138 fob NWE to maintain an even spread against Brent two weeks ago.
